contents.name: Definition 31.33.1 (blowing up b: Proj_X(⊕ I^n) → X, exceptional divisor b^{-1}Z, twists O_{X'}(n) invertible)
Lemma 31.33.2 (affine blowup is Proj of the Rees algebra; covered by the affine blowup algebras A[I/a])
Lemma 31.33.3 (flat base change of blowups is cartesian)
Lemma 31.33.4 (isomorphism off the center; E effective Cartier; O_{X'}(-1)=O_{X'}(E); b^*I → O_{X'}(1) factors through I_E ≅ O_{X'}(1))
Lemma 31.33.5 (universal property: the blowup is the final object among Y → X whose inverse image of Z is an effective Cartier divisor)
Lemma 31.33.6 (a point lies in the chart A[I/a] exactly when the image of a cuts out the exceptional divisor)
Lemma 31.33.7 (blowing up an effective Cartier divisor is the identity)
Lemma 31.33.8 (a reduced scheme has reduced blowup)
Lemma 31.33.9 (an integral scheme with nonzero ideal has integral blowup)
Lemma 31.33.10 (bijection between generic points of the blowup and generic points of X outside Z)
contents.reason: Stacks31.33.10 is a generic-point bijection for general blowups even on reducible bases. cor-blowup-birational-integral-scheme DOES use the unique generic point of its integral base, contrary to the old reason, but proves integral charts plus off-center dense isomorphism directly. The stronger general-bijection claim is not an input or output.

contents.name: Lemma 31.33.11 (pullbacks of effective Cartier divisors and meromorphic functions are defined along a blowup)
Lemma 31.33.12 (blowing up in IJ is the composite of the blowups in I and in b^{-1}J)
Lemma 31.33.13 (a finite type ideal gives a projective blowup with O_{X'}(1) relatively ample)
Lemma 31.33.14 (the composite of two blowups is again a blowup along a finite type ideal)
contents.reason: Stacks31.33.14 represents a composite as one blowup in a finite-type ideal under its conditions. Resolution statements promise a SEQUENCE of point blowups, and their inductive cohomology/contact recurrences need no single-ideal representation.

contents.name: Definition 31.34.1 (strict transform of a scheme over S and of a quasi-coherent sheaf)
Lemma 31.34.2 (the strict transform of X is the blowup of X in the inverse image of Z)
Lemma 31.34.3 (flatness over the center makes the strict transform equal to the base change)
contents.reason: Stacks31.34.3 identifies module/scheme strict transform with pullback when flat along the center. The local closed-subscheme strict-transform theorem proves its quotient by power torsion; no claim discards that quotient under a fiberwise-flat hypothesis. Ordinary blowup flat base change is separately included.

contents.name: Lemma 31.34.4 (strict transforms commute with affine morphisms after blowup)
contents.reason: Stacks31.34.4 is pushforward compatibility for quasi-coherent MODULE strict transforms along an affine morphism. The commissioned closed-subscheme strict transform uses saturated chart quotient rings, not a pushforward of module transforms; its Proof2.1–4.1 does not need this extra compatibility theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 31.34.5 (blowing up in the product of the ideals of Z and an effective Cartier divisor D gives the blowup in Z)
contents.review_evidence: Stacks31.34.5(1) is effective Cartier rescaling on arbitrary schemes. def-blowup-fractional-ideal now supplies the exact ordinary Cartier case: local nonzerodivisor powers identify Rees algebras and unit changes cancel on degree-zero charts, including I=0. The module strict-transform assertion in (2) remains separate and is not commissioned.

contents.name: Lemma31.34.5(2): module strict transforms agree under Cartier rescaling when there are no sections supported on D
contents.reason: The general quasi-coherent module strict-transform invariance in the second assertion is distinct from the included Rees rescaling of blowup schemes. The commissioned strict-transform Definition and closed-immersion theorem concern closed subschemes, and no proof applies that module comparison.

contents.name: Lemma 31.34.6 (description of strict transforms under a composite of two blowups)
contents.reason: Stacks31.34.6 assumes a two-step blowup also equals a single blowup with a specified deleted locus and identifies module/scheme strict transforms. Plane resolution works stepwise with its own schematic strict-transform definition, and makes no consolidation or equality with a single composite center.

contents.name: Lemma 31.34.7 (strict transforms of universally exact sequences stay exact)
contents.reason: Stacks31.34.7 asserts exactness of strict transforms of UNIVERSALLY EXACT module sequences. The module sequences in the blowup cohomology arguments are ordinary exceptional thickenings/twists; their exactness comes from Cartier multiplication and no module strict-transform operation is used.

contents.name: Definition 31.35.1 and Lemmas 31.35.2–31.35.6 (U-admissible blowups: definition, projectivity, base change, composition)
contents.reason: Stacks31.35 defines U-admissibility and its formalism for a specified open U. The ordinary blowup theorem supplies local projectivity/properness and off-center isomorphism directly; no chosen-U admissibility theorem or flattening/descent output is commissioned.

contents.name: Lemmas 31.36.1–31.36.3 (blowing up Fitting ideals: the strict transform of a finite type module becomes locally free)
contents.reason: Stacks31.36.1–3 treat Fitting-ideal blowups, module strict transforms, locally free rank and Tor bounds. No commissioned Statement includes flattening a finite module. Actual normal-cone and surface arguments use regular sequences; the flat-base-change theorem assumes flatness.

contents.name: Theorems 37.16.1–37.16.2 and Lemmas 37.16.3–37.16.8 (critère de platitude par fibres: flatness of a morphism tested on fibres)
contents.reason: Stacks37.16 is fibrewise flatness criteria for local morphisms/modules. The blowup flat-base-change theorem assumes flatness, and local surface projectivity uses explicit coordinate algebras. Flatness over a residue field, where needed, is the direct vector-space fact; no fibrewise criterion is hidden in a proof.

contents.name: Lemma 37.17.1, Remark 37.17.2, Lemma 37.17.3 (blowing up a closed immersion of smooth schemes: X' and E are smooth over the base and E ≅ P(I/I²))
Lemmas 37.18.1–37.18.5 and Remark 37.18.6 (flat modules and relative assassins)
contents.reason: Stacks37.18 treats relative associated points/assassins for flat modules and image properties. No commissioned blowup module Statement involves a relative assassin. Surface contact/finite-support proofs use fixed Noetherian supports and ordinary prime/regular-sequence arguments.

contents.name: §19.4.7–19.4.9 resolving rational maps by blowing up the base ideal, with examples

contents.reason: MITLecture9 complete nonprojective surface separates completeness from projectivity. The commissioned point-blowup/projective-surface arguments establish projectivity from actual embeddings and make no claim that every complete surface is projective. The additional example is not a premise.
